Implementation Plan

# Implementation plan: stop issue text reaching `GITHUB_ENV` in `implement.yml`

The finding is confirmed. In the `Fetch issue metadata` step of `implement.yml` (lines 1642–1658), three values are written to `$GITHUB_ENV` between fixed `EOF` delimiters:
- `ISSUE_SCOPE_LOCK_GLOB`, taken from an issue label.
- `ISSUE_TITLE`, written by the issue author.
- `ISSUE_BODY`, written by the issue author.

Every later step in the job can read these values.

If the body contains a line `EOF`, the variable ends there. Any `KEY=value` lines after it then become real job variables. For example, `ALLOW_BULK_DELETE=true` or `ENFORCE_FILES_TOUCHED=false` would replace the guard settings, which are otherwise set at workflow level from repository variables (lines 51–76).

## Planning ref
- Planning context: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `9d8b2431dee5a105de833a98cbfc80913e485411`, branch `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7`.
- Integration branch metadata: `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7`, so there is no mismatch.
- The code was read in an isolated snapshot of that checkout (local commit `0fde1bf`, "isolated snapshot"). Line numbers below are from that snapshot.

## Automation / wiring
- **Kind of change:** existing code only. No new script, workflow, scheduler entry or supervisor. Nothing goes in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.
- **Trigger:** unchanged. `implement.yml` still runs through `internal-implement.yml` and the consumer `ai-implement.yml` on `/approved`.
- **Database work:** none.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `ISSUE_BODY_FILE` (the existing data file holding the issue body, `${RUNTIME_DIR}/issue_body.txt`, exported at `implement.yml:224`) and the random-delimiter `write_multiline_env` pattern from `plan.yml:883-893`.
Scope-mode justification: The finding's recommendation has two parts, and this plan covers both and nothing else. First, keep issue text in the existing data files rather than `GITHUB_ENV`. Second, read guard settings only from trusted workflow configuration. The root-cause fix removes `ISSUE_BODY` from `GITHUB_ENV`, moves the two readers of that variable to `ISSUE_BODY_FILE`, and writes the two remaining values with an unguessable per-write delimiter. The guard settings are then re-pinned on each guard step from the same `vars.*` expressions the workflow already uses. That is under 30 YAML lines and adds no dependency or interface, so by the Boil the Lake rule and §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > …) the complete fix is chosen.

The same class of bug was searched for elsewhere:
- In `.github/workflows`, `workflow-templates` and `.github/actions`, only these three `<KEY><<EOF` writes exist, all in this step.
- `plan.yml` already uses a non-fixed delimiter, so it is not changed here.

## 1. Files likely to change
1. `.github/workflows/implement.yml` (the only workflow; currently 331,513 bytes, far below the 480,000-byte guard).
2. `tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py`: update existing contracts and add regression tests.
3. `changelog.d/6504-implement-issue-body-github-env-injection.md`: new fragment, `<!-- changelog: security -->`, following CLAUDE.md §20.
4. `agents.md`: one sentence next to the "Integration-ref trust boundary" paragraph stating that issue title and body text never go to `GITHUB_ENV` with a fixed delimiter, and that the body travels only through `ISSUE_BODY_FILE`.

No files under `scripts/` change. Every guard script already reads its settings from the environment, and step-level `env:` takes precedence over `GITHUB_ENV`.

## 2. Changes in `implement.yml`

### A. `Fetch issue metadata` step (about lines 1590–1658), the root-cause fix
- Keep reading `ISSUE_BODY` from `ISSUE_META_FILE` into a shell variable, and keep `printf '%s\n' "${ISSUE_BODY}" > "${ISSUE_BODY_FILE}"` exactly as it is (line 1640).
- **Remove** the `ISSUE_BODY<<EOF` / `"${ISSUE_BODY}"` / `EOF` lines from the `>> "$GITHUB_ENV"` block. The body never enters the job environment.
- Add a step-local function `write_untrusted_multiline_env KEY VALUE`. Check that the name is not already used anywhere in `implement.yml`; it currently is not. The function:
  - builds a delimiter from 16 random bytes: `ghadelimiter_$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')`;
  - fails closed with an `::error::` line and `exit 1` if the hex part is not exactly 32 hex characters;
  - fails closed if VALUE contains the delimiter (`case "${value}" in *"${delim}"*)`);
  - writes `printf '%s<<%s\n%s\n%s\n' key delim value delim >> "$GITHUB_ENV"`. Using `printf` instead of `echo` also stops a title such as `-n` or `-e` from being misread as an `echo` option.
- Write `ISSUE_SCOPE_LOCK_GLOB` and `ISSUE_TITLE` through this function. Their values do not change.
- `ISSUE_NUMBER`, `ISSUE_URL` and `PR_BASE_BRANCH` stay as single-line `KEY=value` writes. They come from GitHub-issued data and the validated integration ref, not from text the issue author writes.
- Update the `TRUST BOUNDARY` comment to say the body is never exported to `GITHUB_ENV`, why, and the reference `#6504`.

### B. `Detect smoke test and silence Telegram alerts` step, alt-model parse (line 1734)
- Replace `printf '%s' "${ISSUE_BODY}" | grep -oE …` with `grep -oE '<same regex>' "${ISSUE_BODY_FILE:-/dev/null}" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed -E … || true`.
- If the file is missing or unreadable, the result is empty, and the existing `::warning::` fallback to the workflow `MODEL_EDITOR` still applies. The shape check and 128-character cap stay as they are.

### C. `Build implementation context` step (line 2071)
- Replace `printf '%s\n\n' "${ISSUE_BODY}"` with a check that `ISSUE_BODY_FILE` exists as a regular file (otherwise `::error::` and `exit 1`), followed by `cat "${ISSUE_BODY_FILE}"; echo`.
- The output is byte-for-byte the same. The file holds `body\n` (written with `printf '%s\n'`), so `cat` plus `echo` gives `body\n\n`, the same bytes as before.

### D. Pin guard settings on the guard steps (defense in depth)
Add a step-level `env:` block to these four steps:
- `Preflight destructive-commit guard` (line 3470, `id: preflight_destructive_guard`)
- `Protect workflow files from implementation edits` (line 4332)
- `Commit changes` (`id: commit_changes`, which runs `implement_commit_changes.sh`)
- `Destructive-commit guard — label + alert on rejection`, which runs `implement_handle_guard_block.sh` and uses these values in its messages

Each block re-declares these variables using the **same** expression as the workflow-level `env:` at lines 51–76, copied character for character:
- `ALLOW_BULK_DELETE`
- `BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD`
- `BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD_MD`
- `ENFORCE_FILES_TOUCHED`
- `ALLOW_OUT_OF_SCOPE_FILES`
- `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS`
- `WRITE_GUARDS_ENABLED`
- `SCOPE_LOCK_LABEL_ENABLED`

If a step already has an `env:` block, add the keys to it without reordering existing keys. Do **not** pin `UNBLOCK_BULK_DELETE_OVERRIDE` or `UNBLOCK_BULK_DELETE_PATHS`; the trusted step at line 1988 sets those through `GITHUB_ENV` on purpose.

Add a comment saying that step-level `env:` takes precedence over `GITHUB_ENV`, so an injected job variable can no longer weaken these guards, with the reference `#6504`. Use 2-space YAML indentation.

## 3. Data structures affected
- The job environment no longer contains `ISSUE_BODY`. No step after `Fetch issue metadata` reads it, and no script does either. Repository-wide search: `scripts/semantic_cache.py:69` contains the string only as literal text. Readers in `orchestrate_parse_and_post_answer.sh` and `workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh` belong to other workflows and use `ISSUE_TITLE`, not `ISSUE_BODY`.
- `ISSUE_TITLE` and `ISSUE_SCOPE_LOCK_GLOB` keep their names and values; only the delimiter changes. No identifiers are renamed (§10).

## 4. API or interface changes
None. No workflow inputs, outputs, log prefixes or repository variables change, and no GitHub API calls are added (§14).

## Decisions

### D1 — Remove the body from `GITHUB_ENV` instead of escaping it
- **Chosen:** delete the `ISSUE_BODY` export and read `ISSUE_BODY_FILE` in the two places that used the variable.
- **Alternatives considered:** keep the export with a random delimiter; base64-encode the body into the environment.
- **Why:** the recommendation says to keep issue text in data files. Large untrusted text in the environment also reaches every later process (Codex launches, helpers). The data file already exists and holds the same bytes.

### D2 — A random delimiter for the remaining author-written values
- **Chosen:** a per-write delimiter from 16 bytes of `/dev/urandom`, plus a fail-closed check that the value does not contain it.
- **Alternatives considered:** strip line breaks from the title and write `KEY=value`; reuse `plan.yml`'s `date +%s%N`/`$RANDOM` delimiter.
- **Why:** the value is kept exactly. The delimiter cannot be predicted, unlike a timestamp-based one. The containment check makes a collision fail the step instead of writing variables.

### D3 — Pin guard settings on the guard steps
- **Chosen:** step-level `env:` that repeats the workflow-level `vars.*` expressions.
- **Alternatives considered:** fix only the root cause; have the guard scripts re-read repository variables through the API.
- **Why:** it matches the second half of the recommendation, behaviour is identical (same expressions), there are no API calls, and step-level `env:` beats `GITHUB_ENV`. It protects the guards even if another step leaks job variables in future.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundary:** the issue title, body and labels are untrusted input. After this change, author-written text reaches later steps only as a data file (the body) or as a value framed by an unguessable delimiter (title and scope glob). It can never become a new job variable such as `ALLOW_BULK_DELETE`, `ENFORCE_FILES_TOUCHED`, `BASH_ENV` or `LD_PRELOAD`.
